originalMetadata.description: This magnificent plum vase (meiping) derives its name from being used to hold a branch from a flowering plum tree. summary: 施釉炻器，带化妆土彩绘装饰，吉州窑
description: 江西省中部的吉州窑窑口为与中国其他窑口竞争而生产深色瓷器，因此吉州窑陶工极具创造力。他们的部分作品是在器物上施一层白色化妆土，并在其上绘制具有强烈视觉效果的醒目图案。这种引人注目的水波纹设计令人称奇，画师将瓶的整个表面转化为动态翻滚的水体，并以翻腾的浪花加以凸显。吉州窑瓷器在长江三角洲下游城市（包括南京、上海、常州、泰州）以及安徽省、韩国和日本均有出土。吉州窑烧制时，化妆土涂层和镶嵌装饰会呈现柔和的象牙色，而暴露的胎体则呈现温暖的桂皮色。
history: 中国江西省永和镇，元代（1271–1368）

originalMetadata.technique: glazed stoneware with slip painted decoration, Jizhou ware
originalMetadata.description: Jizhou ware kilns in central Jiangxi province produced a dark ware in competition with other kilns in China and so Jizhou potters were highly inventive. Part of their work is a ware covered with a white slip over which they painted bold graphic designs of great visual effect. This striking wave design is remarkable in the way the painter transformed the entire surface of the vase into dynamically rolling masses of water, highlighted by cresting waves. Jizhou wares were excavated in cities of the lower Yangzi delta, including Nanjing, Shanghai, Changzhou, Taizhou, as well as Anhui province, Korea, and Japan.

name: 青花双狮头罐
description: 此罐因其鲜明的造型轮廓、浓艳的青蓝色泽以及坚劲利落的纹饰线条而备受称赞，是元代青花瓷的经典范例。此类器物最迟在14世纪30年代便已生产，兼供国内（宫廷与民间）及海外贸易使用。该件器物见证了因贸易而在中国与大蒙古国其他地区之间展开的艺术观念与工艺技术的交流。用于釉下青花装饰的钴料进口自伊朗，可能出自卡尚。如此器所见，以缠枝花卉为底衬的云肩凤纹带，也是伊利汗国时期（1256–1353年）伊朗装饰艺术中常见的一种艺术语汇。该器肩部白釉上刻划有“宫”与“南”字样，表明其曾藏于宫廷内的特定场所。

originalMetadata.title: Jar with Lion-Head Handles
culture: China, Jiangxi Province, Jingdezhen, Yuan dynasty (1271–1368)
originalMetadata.description: Appreciated for its strong profile, brilliant blue color, and firm delineation of the decorative patterns, this jar is a classic example of Yuan dynasty blue-and-white ware. This type of ware was produced no later than the 1330s for both domestic use (the court and common people alike) and overseas trade. This example testifies to the transmission of artistic ideas and techniques between China and the rest of the great Mongol Empire as a result of trade. The cobalt that was used for the blue underglaze decoration was imported from Iran, likely from Kashan. The band of cloud-collar motifs with phoenixes set against floral grounds, as shown here, is an artistic vocabulary that can also be found in Iranian decorative arts of the Ilkhanid period (1256–1353).
originalMetadata.did_you_know: The characters for "palace" and "south" are scratched into the white glaze on the vessel's shoulder, suggesting that it was once kept in a specific location in a palace.

originalMetadata.title: Prunus Vase (Meiping) with Blossoming Lotus
culture: China, Jiangxi Province, Jingdezhen kilns, Ming dynasty (1368–1644)
originalMetadata.technique: Porcelain with polychrome glazes, Fahua ware
originalMetadata.description:
According to 11th-century poet Zhou Dunyi, “all people like peonies, but I alone like the lotus because it emerges from the mud unstained.” The lotus is a symbol of purity and popular among Chinese literati and in Buddhism. This vase shows lotus flowers rising from the water’s surface depicted in elegant yet simple ripples.

Made in a kiln at Jingdezhen in southern China, this vase is an example of the fahua technique—decoration with raised outlines produced by squeezing clay from a tube onto the vase’s surface. Colors are applied to fill the outlines before firing.
originalMetadata.did_you_know: The shoulders of the vase are decorated with ruyi-shaped clouds.

The clear glaze over the white body has a luster and purity; the white color radiates with a soft glow like melting snow, described by the Chinese connoisseurs as tianbai, or "sweetwhite." Tianbai wares were produced for use in imperial offerings and have always been considered a great achievement of the Yongle period.

culture: China, Jiangxi province, Jingdezhen kilns, Ming dynasty (1368-1644)
originalMetadata.technique: Porcelain with sweet-white (tianbai; 甜白) glaze
originalMetadata.description: White was a ritual color used in Buddhist ceremonies, as well as the color of mourning. This jar is made of two molded halves that were joined where the vessel’s middle section shows a raised line. It is covered by a silky white glaze called “sweet-white” (tianbai; 甜白). The jar may have been used as a planter, a vase for flowers, or it may have held incense sticks on a home altar.
originalMetadata.did_you_know: Tianbai, or sweet-white glaze, was developed to accommodate the Yongle emperor’s (reigned 1403–24) preference for white ceramics.

summary: 青白釉瓷（施淡青白釉瓷器）
description: 这件斗笠碗（锥形碗）与另一件浅而宽的碗（藏品号 CMA 2020.183）均以手工刻划出看似水波、云纹或花卉折枝的纹饰。这些图案均富有吉祥寓意：波浪与云纹能带来滋润田地的雨水，花草植物则常与人类美德之美联系在一起。刻花与梳划纹是在施釉前，用木制工具在未烧制的生坯（皮革硬度坯体）上迅速划刻而成的。施釉后，釉料积聚在刻纹凹入部位，使图案更清晰显现。青白瓷并非用于御用，是最早实现量产的瓷器品种之一，并成为受欢迎的外销商品。

originalMetadata.title: Bowl with Carved Design
originalMetadata.description: This conical bowl and the shallow and wide one (CMA 2020.183) are both hand-incised with decoration suggesting waves, clouds, or floral sprays. All of these motifs had auspicious meaning: waves and clouds bring rain that fertilizes the fields, and flowers and plants were often associated with the beauty of human virtues. The carved and combed designs were swiftly cut with a wooden tool into the unfired leather-hard body before glazing. Once the glaze was applied, it pooled in the incised areas rendering the design more visible.
originalMetadata.did_you_know: Never intended for imperial use, qingbai ware was among the first mass-produced porcelain types and became a popular export.

description: 单色黄釉瓷最早出现于明代，是技术进步、国家礼制需求与品味追求相结合的产物。底部带有正德（1505–1521年）年款；正德朝以其高品质的御用瓷器，以及一位英年早逝、沉溺享乐的皇帝而闻名。唯有隶属于宫廷的景德镇作坊才被允许使用御用年款。多数学者认为，单色黄釉器皿专供皇室使用或用作外交礼品，因此该颜色常被称为“御黄”。

originalMetadata.title: Yellow-Glazed Bowl
culture: China, Jiangxi province, Jingdezhen kilns, Ming dynasty (1368–1644), Zhengde mark and reign (1505–21)
originalMetadata.description: Monochrome yellow–glazed porcelain appears first during the Ming dynasty and is the combined result of technological advancement, the requirements of state rituals, and aspirations of taste. The base bears a mark of the Zhengde (正德) reign period, renowned for its high-quality imperial porcelain, and a pleasure-seeking emperor who died in his youth. Imperial marks were permitted to be applied only by Jingdezhen workshops affiliated with the court. Most scholars believe that yellow monochrome ware was reserved for the use of the imperial household or served as diplomatic gifts. The color is therefore often called “imperial yellow.”
originalMetadata.did_you_know: Zhengde–marked bowls of this so-called imperial yellow type are also preserved in the National Palace Museum in Taipei and the Topkapi Saray, Istanbul, once the palace of the Ottoman sultans.

name: 觚形瓶，出自五件套组
originalName: Beaker-shaped vase, from a five-piece garniture
summary: 透明无色釉下钴料彩绘（青花）
description: 觚形瓶，为五件套组（F1980.190-194）中的两件之一。青花。胎：白瓷。釉：透明长石釉。装饰：以釉下钴蓝彩绘，撇口颈部绘有与棒槌瓶/观音瓶（F1980.190、F1980.191、F1980.192）相似的宫廷场景，中段与下段绘有庭院环境中的其他仕女；各段以人字纹边饰分隔。另附此前未记录的木座。

sources.title: Beaker-shaped vase, from a five-piece garniture

notes.label: Description
notes.content: Beaker-shaped vase, one of two in a five-piece garniture (F1980.190-194). Blue-and-white.

notes.label: Description
notes.content: Decoration: painted in underglaze cobalt blue with court scene similar to baluster vases F1980.190, F1980.191, F1980.192 on flaring neck, other court ladies in garden setting on lower and middle sections. Sections divided by herringbone borders.

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: Mrs. B. F. Jones Jr. (d. 1941), Pittsburgh and Sewickley Heights, Pennsylvania, purchased from Duveen Brothers in 1916 [2]

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: Sale, New York, Parke-Bernet Galleries, Inc., “Art Property and Furnishings of the Palatial Residence of the Late Mrs. B.F. Jones Jr, Sewickley Heights, PA,” November 27, 1941, lot 670 (ill.): “Important Blue and White Five-Piece Garniture, K’ang-hsi”

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: Myron S. Falk, Sr. (1878-1945), Greenwich, Connecticut, purchased through Edward Wells at the Parke-Bernet Sale, Inc., New York, November 27, 1941 [3]

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: Myron S. Falk, Jr. (1906-1992), New York, given by Myron S. Falk, Sr. in the 1940s [4]

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: Freer Gallery of Art, given by Myron S. Falk, Jr. and his sisters Mrs. Mildred F. Loew and Mrs. Eleanor F. Lenzner in 1980

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: [1] The garniture appears in an undated Duveen Brothers black-and-white stock photo, which bears the handwritten notations: "1849/29761, Height of Vases 18 1/2 ins., beakers 17 1/2 ins." and "61" in the lower left corner, and "A set of 5 Blue & White Nankin vases & beakers", in the lower right corner. See Getty Research Institute, Los Angeles, Duveen Brothers records, Duveen Brothers stock documentation from the dealer’s library, 1829-1965. Series I. Photograph albums, 1871-1956. Series I.A. Stock albums, 1907-1954; ID/Accession Number: 2007.D.1 (bx.1-9), China books, vol. 3, p. 61. Persistent link: http://hdl.handle.net/10020/cat717039.

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: [2] The purchase was recorded on September 19, 1941 in the Duveen Brothers' collector file for B. F. Jones Jr., as one of the "Objects sold directly to Mrs. B.F. Jones, Jr.", during the year 1916. There it is described as "A Garniture of Five Pieces of Old Chinese Porcelain of fine quality. Kang Hsi period. Consisting of 3 Vases with Covers, and 2 Beaker-shaped Vases, decorated with figures of Lange Eleisen flowers, etc.", and a price of $9,000 is noted. See Getty Research Institute, Los Angeles, Duveen Brothers records, 1876-1981 (bulk 1909-1964). Series II. Correspondence and papers. Series II.I. Collectors' files: Jones, B. F., Jr., 1, ca. 1917-1941, ID/Accession number: 960015, (bx.472,f.3), p. 2. Persistent link: http://hdl.handle.net/10020/960015b472f003.

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: [3] The object is listed in an invoice issued by Wells Objects of Art Specialist in Chinese Antiquities to Myron S. Falk on November 28, 1941, copy in object file.

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: A copy of the 1941 auction catalogue preserved in the Museum Library bears Myron S. Falk Sr.’s handwritten notations: “Welles will bid $1050 for M.S.F. Valued $3-4,000. Mrs. Jones paid Duveen Bros. $15,000", in the left margin and "Sold for $800. to M. S. F." in the right margin. The accompanying plate illustrating the garniture bears the handwritten notation: "In my opinion covers do not belong—but extremely fine set! Extremely rare in garniture form and without defects". See also “Art Sale Brings $14,135: K’an-shi Garniture is sold for $750…,” New York Times (November 27, 1941).

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: [4] The objects were gifted by Myron S. Falk, Sr. to his son, Myron S. Falk, Jr., see Page Report, dated September 18, 1995, in object file.

notes.label: Provenance
notes.content: The objects were initially included in Sotheby-Parke-Bernet Galleries’s Sale “Fine Chinese Works of Art” on May 8, 1980 as lot 261 (color ill.) and then taken out of the sale.
